notes: ACCESS AND ROBOTS - READ THIS FIRST, IT IS A JUDGEMENT CALL AND IT IS DISCLOSED IN FULL. https://www.noon.com/robots.txt was fetched before any other request. It contains SEVEN groups: '*' (Disallow: /_svc/, Disallow: /_vs/, Allow: /), BadBot (Disallow: /), and then GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot, each of which is 'Allow: /' with NO Disallow line at all. The exact ClaudeBot directive is: 'User-agent: ClaudeBot' / 'Allow: /'. Under RFC 9309 s2.2.1 a crawler MUST use the most specific matching group and IGNORE the others, so for us the governing group is ClaudeBot / Allow: / - an explicit, deliberate opt-IN, the same pattern BATCH_BRIEF s1.4 records for H&M, Conforama and Westwing DE ('a site naming Claude and then saying Allow: / is an explicit opt-IN'). Noon has clearly written this file to name AI crawlers individually and admit them while keeping its internal service paths out of general crawlers. On that reading the counts below were taken from www.noon.com/_svc/catalog/api/v3/u/... , the storefront's OWN catalogue service - the one the PLP itself renders from, which WORKER_BRIEF s4 explicitly names as the correct source for a client-rendered listing. If the run owner prefers the stricter reading in which the '*' group's '/_svc/' Disallow is treated as binding on every agent, then every figure in rows[] must be treated as unverified; the independent cross-check described below was run precisely so that judgement can be made without re-crawling. WHAT WAS NOT TOUCHED: api-app.noon.com, the OTHER host the page calls (path prefix /_vs/), was NOT used. Its robots.txt returns HTTP 503 on repeated tries, so its permission is unverifiable, and /_vs/ is disallowed for '*' on the main host; per BATCH_BRIEF s1.3 (robots is per-host) and the SR 145 non-laundering principle, no request was made to it and no reader/proxy was pointed at anything that would fetch it. No browser automation, no third-party CORS proxy, no campaign parameter. All requests went through probe.fetch() fingerprint rotation and returned HTTP 200; there is no bot wall on noon.com. No Crawl-delay is declared; probe.py's 2 s per-host gap was kept throughout. TREE: entry point is Noon's own navigation - homepage > Home & Kitchen > Bath (https://www.noon.com/uae-en/home-and-kitchen/bath-16182/). The listing grid is client-rendered, but the PLP's left-hand Category facet IS server-rendered as a full nested tree, and that is where the hierarchy came from: 86 Bath nodes read straight out of the delivered HTML, cross-checked against the child links on the department pages. Each node's identity was then confirmed from the catalogue payload's own breadcrumbs array and canonical_url - EVERY node is self-canonical (no alias redirects) and every breadcrumb matched the node requested. Recovered tree: Bath > Bathroom Accessories > {Holders & Dispensers (10 children), Toilet Accessories (5), Bathroom Mirrors, Bath Mats & Rugs, Drain Stoppers, Shower Curtain Rods, Bathtub Trays, Bathroom Accessory Sets, Bathtub Mats, Bath Ensembles, Bath Pillows, Bath Stools, Towel Warmers, Hand Dryers}; Bathroom Storage & Organisation (10); Bath Hardware (11); Towels (8); Bath Linen (3); Bathroom Aids & Safety (8); Bathroom Lighting (4); Bathroom Scales (1); Kids Bath Towels / Kids Bathroom Accessories / Kids Bath Rugs. Outside Bath: Furniture > Bathroom Furniture (3), Household Supplies > Household Cleaning > Bathroom Cleaners, Furniture > Bedroom > Vanities & Vanity Benches, Tools & Home Improvement > Rough Plumbing (faucet-parts, toilet-parts). All were walked and are accounted for in rows[] or review[]. THE CAP TRAP, FOUND AND DEFEATED (BATCH_BRIEF s3, the OTTO lesson). Noon's PAGINATION is hard-capped. Probing the public HTML listing with ?page=N shows that page 50 and beyond return a fixed fallback set - pages 50, 200, 1000 and 5000 of Toilet Plungers returned the IDENTICAL 50 SKUs - so the last reachable real page is 49 and any page-walk tops out at 49 x 50 = 2,450. The Bath department itself, which plainly holds far more than 2,450 listings, ends at exactly the same page 49. That is precisely the OTTO signature: a round figure repeated across nodes of visibly different size is a CAP, not a count. The payload confirms it: nbPages is capped at 50 while nbHits is not. Every recorded figure is nbHits, the UNCAPPED field, never nbPages and never a page-walk. QTY PROOF - four independent checks, all passed. (1) nbHits is STABLE ACROSS PAGE SIZES: every one of the 92 nodes was queried twice, at limit=50 and limit=100, and nbHits was identical (this is the Sostrene Grene page-size-dependence test; only one node, Toilet Brush, moved, and only by live churn - see (4)). (2) nbPages == min(50, ceil(nbHits/limit)) holds for BOTH limits on ALL 92 nodes - verified programmatically - which is the lastPage-vs-ceil cross-check the brief demands and which simultaneously proves the 50 is a cap sitting on top of an uncapped nbHits. On Towel Warmers this was walked out explicitly: limit=1 -> nbPages 50 (capped), limit=20 -> 16 = ceil(308/20), limit=50 -> 7 = ceil(308/50), limit=100 -> 4 = ceil(308/100). (3) ENUMERATION TO EXHAUSTION on a node small enough to finish: Towel Warmers paginated through the catalogue service gave six full pages of 50 plus a seventh page of exactly 8 = 308, which equals nbHits exactly. (4) The figures DISCRIMINATE across four orders of magnitude, from 22 (Sitz Bath) to 98,904 (Towel Hooks), with no repeated round number. TWO HONEST CAVEATS ON THE NUMBERS. (a) They are POINT-IN-TIME. Noon is a live marketplace and nbHits drifts by ~0.1% between calls minutes apart (Toothbrush Holders read 78,448 then 78,383; Toilet Paper Holders 37,134 then 37,131). Every recorded value is the figure read in this session. (b) The public HTML page must NOT be scraped for these counts and was not: the rendered grid appends recommendation-carousel products, proved directly - on Towel Warmers page 7 the catalogue service returns the 8 real remaining items while the HTML page yields 32 SKUs, the 8 real ones plus 24 carousel items, which is why a naive HTML page-walk gave a wrong 332 against the true 308. DEDUP (OPTION 1): already_extracted() was run on all 92 nodes and on five URL variants of each (trailing-slash, bare noon.com host, /uae-ar/ Arabic locale, /ae-en/ form) - 460 checks. noon.com IS in exclusion_index.json with 61 URLs from the Final.xlsx Home Decor pass, INCLUDING the whole /home-decor/mirrors-16780/ branch (Mirrors, Wall Mounted Mirrors, Floor Mirrors, Mirror Sets, Tabletop Vanity Mirrors, Vanity Mirrors), which is why no decorative-mirror node is touched here; the Bathroom Mirrors node recorded in rows is a DIFFERENT category under Bath (/bath-16182/bathroom-accessories/bathroom-mirrors/) and is a clean miss. THREE hits were returned, all from Furniture.xlsx and all in the Bathroom Furniture / vanity area exactly as the brief predicted: Bathroom Sets, Medicine Cabinets and Vanities & Vanity Benches. All three are in review[], none in rows[]. Over The Toilet Storage, the third child of Bathroom Furniture, is a clean miss and is therefore the one leaf recorded from that branch. Locale blind spot (b)/(c): Noon runs /uae-en/ and /uae-ar/ on the same host and separate country hosts are separate storefronts; the /uae-ar/ form of every node was dedup-checked and misses, and only /uae-en/ was ever fetched. ROWS: 51 leaves under 8 grouping rows. Bathroom Accessories, Toilet Accessories, Bath Hardware, Bathroom Storage & Organisation and Bathroom Aids & Safety are all core rules 6/13/14/17 content. Bathroom Mirrors is recorded under rule 10/11 (mirror is the primary type; the Vanity Lighting node next door is routed to Lighting). Bathtub Mats is recorded under rule 16's rubber/anti-slip branch while its sibling Bath Mats & Rugs is routed to Textile - a split the site's own taxonomy makes for us. Bathroom Aids & Safety is included as bathroom-specific safety fittings (grab bars, non-slip shower strips, shower chairs, toilet frames, elevated toilet seats - the last squarely inside rule 14's Toilet Seats - bathtub lifts, sitz baths, shower thermometers/alarms). THREE DUPLICATE NAV PATHS WERE COLLAPSED (rule 28 / BATCH_BRIEF s4d), proved by identical 50-SKU page-1 sets and lock-step totals: Toothbrush Holders, Toilet Paper Holders and Toilet Brush Holders each exist under both Bathroom Accessories and Bathroom Storage & Organisation. One record each; the alias is in review[]. A fourth, Holders & Dispensers > Toilet Paper Holders (23,556), overlaps the recorded node by 35 of 50 page-1 SKUs but carries a different total, so it too was withheld rather than double-counted, and is disclosed with its figure. MARKETPLACE CONTAMINATION, DISCLOSED: because Noon is a third-party marketplace, some category grids carry seller mis-listings (the Canisters grid surfaces sitz baths and hair oil; Kids Bathroom Accessories surfaces water balloons and baby ear stickers). The recorded numbers are Noon's own totals for its own category URLs, obtained from the payload its PLP renders from; they are not a claim that every listing inside is correctly categorised by the seller. Bath Ensembles was withheld entirely on these grounds (rule 29) because its majority content is laundry and washing-machine storage. EXCLUDED and why: Towels branch (176,877 with 8 children) + Bath Linen (55,927 with Shower Curtains 46,831, Bath Slippers 8,231, Bath Robes 505) + Bath Mats & Rugs 46,570 + Kids Bath Towels 3,586 + Kids Bath Rugs 1,743 -> Textile (rules 15/16/20); Bathroom Lighting 12,312 with its 4 children -> Lighting (rules 11/19, no duplication into Bathroom); Hamper 1,616 -> Storage/Laundry; Bathroom Scales 6,490 and Digital Scales 5 -> measuring appliances, not Bathroom (rule 2, as SR 15); Bathroom Cleaners 16,663 -> cleaning chemicals (as SR 80); Bath Ensembles 8,585 -> LOW confidence mixed node; Bathroom Sets, Medicine Cabinets, Vanities & Vanity Benches -> already in Furniture.xlsx; Faucet Parts 40,328 and Toilet Parts 35,134 -> plumbing spares in the Tools department. All parent hubs are grouping rows with blank qty and blank link (rules 24/38) and their figures appear in review[] as evidence only - they overlap their children and must never be summed or reconciled. Nothing was estimated; no URL, count or category was invented.
